lesson_title: The How-Many-Steps Question: Exponentials and Logs
hook_text: A chain message doubles every hour. The log button on your calculator answers one question: how many hours until it reaches everyone?
clip_script: One person gets a chain message. Every hour it doubles: one, two, four, eight. After x hours, 2 to the x people — that is the exponential, doubling written as a power. Now flip the question. Not how many people after 3 hours — how many HOURS until 8 people? Three. And the notation for that answer is log base 2 of 8. A logarithm is just the how-many-steps question. Log base 2 of 32? Five doublings. Log base 10 of 1000? Three. Log base 2 of a quarter? Minus 2 — two steps backwards. And log of a negative number? How many doublings turn one person into minus four people? None. Ever. That question has no answer, which is why the log graph slams into a wall at the y axis and never crosses it. Exponential and log are the same table read in opposite directions — mirror twins across the diagonal y equals x. Master one sentence, a log is an exponent, and the whole topic opens.
visual_style: A phone screen with a chain message multiplying across a contact web, counts doubling in glowing nodes, then the animation reversing step by step as the log question rewinds it, a dashed wall rising along the y axis.
mood: Viral-fast, then a clean rewind, one hard wall.
pacing: Accelerating doubles, a snap reverse on the flip question, steady certainty on the wall and the mirror.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make every log question answer itself.
